items.summary: The Contract change mechanics match every acceptance criterion except that the billed payer is the Booking's single payer, where the story now says the Procedure's own payer (US-11.2.2, Donald 17 Nov).
items.requirement_says: Until the List is AUTHORISED the anaesthetist changes a Procedure's Contract with no reason. A typed price is cleared, recorded RVG detail is kept, and the RVG code fills only when empty. Every change is audited and flagged at office review. Moving off an insurer Contract to No contract · RVG bills the Procedure's payer (the patient or someone else). The anaesthetist can never move a Procedure onto or off a prepaid Contract and is never offered one.
items.prototype_does: setProcedureContract is gated by editRefusal, which refuses only an AUTHORISED List and allows ACTIVE and SUBMITTED ones. It asks no reason and goes through contractPickRefusal and contractChangeRefusal. applyContractChange clears priceOverride, enteredPrice and railAnswers and fills the RVG code only when empty. withRvgRowChange keeps the recorded RVG detail. One audited 'procedure.contract' entry holds before and after, and any earlier office approval stamp is dropped. Review shows the changed-by flag. contractChangeRefusal blocks an anaesthetist onto or off a prepaid Contract. ProcedureContractRow shows 'Set by the office' in place of Change on a prepaid Procedure. The rail lists no prepaid Contract for the anaesthetist, only a greyed, non-selectable 'Prepaid · Set by the office' payment-type answer. No contract · RVG bills payerCounterparty(booking), the single Booking.payer. Procedure has no payer field.
missing_or_wrong: 'Pre-approval falls through' now bills the Procedure's own payer. The prototype bills Booking.payer through whoIsBilled.ts payerCounterparty and billablePartyForProcedure, and the Procedure interface in types.ts has no payer. Two Procedures on one Booking cannot bill different people. For a single-payer Booking the result matches the AC.

The payer is edited on the Booking (setBookingPayer, 'booking-payer-row' in BookingDetailBody), and there is no Procedure-level 'Paid by' line or offer to copy a change to the Booking's other Procedures. This belongs to US-11.2.2 rather than this story, but it is what makes this AC only partly met.

The greyed 'Prepaid · Set by the office' payment-type answer on the anaesthetist's rail is consistent with Donald's 16 Nov ruling in the code comment, because no prepaid Contract is offered. It is not a gap.
items.verify_note: I re-opened the story, US-11.2.2, setProcedureContract, editRefusal, contractRail, ProcedureContractRow, whoIsBilled and types.ts. The Contract-change behaviour is as the reviewer described. The only real gap is the payer on each Procedure, and nothing implemented contradicts the story. Booking.payer is a deliberate earlier reading, so Partial fits better than Contradicts. I kept size S for this story, because the payer move itself belongs to US-11.2.2 (cross-epic M or L) and this story only needs a re-check afterwards. I did not check the screenshots listed in the frontmatter.

Separately, addBillingLine adds fixed or rate x time lines with a free-text description to a Procedure before authorisation. Invoice.kind is only standard|prePayment; a negative price override is blocked as a credit note 'this system never raises'.

MISSING: bundling an event onto another invoice for the same billable party in the run; the addendum always gets its own invoice

MISSING: invoice tick box (cleared = not invoiced)

MISSING: event billable party differing from the Procedure's

items.summary: Five pricing kinds, undated rate and discount, fixed price by range and open price all work, and the per-Contract override setting exists, but it is never acted on: the anaesthetist's price change is the old always-available Adj $ / Charge $ card with a mandatory reason, shown on any Contract including fixed and prepaid. Status Verify (3); OQ-136 (holder references) is open and the prototype follows the interim reading.
items.requirement_says: Five pricing kinds (RVG at anaesthetist's rate, at Contract's rate, less discount, fixed via price ranges, open price only for fallbacks). A per-Contract setting lets the anaesthetist override the price on RVG-priced Contracts only, with no reason needed and RVG detail kept; without it the price is read-only and the anaesthetist cannot discount; fixed-price and prepaid Contracts never carry it and the anaesthetist cannot change their price.
items.prototype_does: Kinds and maths implemented (feeFor by kind, rangeInForce, enteredPrice for open, discount as its own invoice line, fixed price asks for no times or modifiers). Editor offers 'Anaesthetist may override the price' on RVG kinds with overrideOnlyRvg refusal. OverrideCard is rendered unconditionally in the capture block and writes fixedFee or dollarAdjustment with a mandatory reason; validateBookingForBilling fails an override with no reason; a fixedFee override also clears 'Needs a price' on any Contract.
missing_or_wrong: Anaesthetist's override is not gated by Contract.anaesthetistMayOverridePrice: OverrideCard shows on every Contract, so a fixed-price or prepaid Contract's price can be replaced by the anaesthetist and an RVG Contract without the setting can be discounted (violates 'Editable setting' and 'Fixed price never overridden' ACs).
Override requires a mandatory reason (OverrideCard reasonValid; validateBookingForBilling 'Give a reason for the price override.'); AC says no reason needed.
When the setting is off the price should be read-only with no discount control; the prototype has no such read-only state.
Seed has no rvgDiscount Contract, so the 'Fixed discount' AC can only be shown by creating one in the editor (minor).
evidence: aa-prototype/src/domain/billing/contracts.ts:110 ('Phase 24 acts on it'), :326 (overrideOnlyRvg), :494 (fixedFee override satisfies needs-price)
searched: anaesthetistMayOverridePrice readers in capture/booking UI -> none

Added the missing-discount-seed note and that a fixedFee override clears needsPrice, which lets an override stand in for a typed price. Size M stands: gate the card by contract, drop the reason, read-only state, reseed typed-price beats, demo guide.

The line is a non-RVG BillingLine (chargeBasis fixed) on the Procedure, billed with the Procedure's invoice at List authorisation. There is no event type anywhere in the domain, no ACC code preset or master, and no separate next-run billing for such items.

Wrong billing timing: the line rides on the Procedure's invoice at List authorisation; catalogue says events bill in the next billing run, bundled where possible, else own invoice (OQ-121)

No event invoice tick box, no event billable party with 'same as Procedure' tick, so bundling-vs-own-invoice behaviour cannot be shown
Admin/caller-on-behalf entry of a pre-op event does not exist (no event concept)
Presets, when built, need a 'to be confirmed' marker because OQ-12 part 1 (are the codes right) is still open
Story screenshots (web/mobile-acc-preop.png) depict the superseded flat-fee line and would need retaking once events exist

items.summary: The epic states its own rules (prepaid Contract trigger or typed amount, holding account, nothing further after the procedure); the prototype implements the older payment-category, estimate or deposit, payee-is-anaesthetist, balance-netting model.
items.requirement_says: A Procedure is prepaid by picking a prepaid Contract (or typing an amount for one Booking); the system invoices the payer, holds the money in the AA Holding account until the procedure is done, and transfers it to the anaesthetist who did the List. The prepaid amount is the price and nothing further is raised automatically.
items.prototype_does: A Procedure is prepaid when billingRoute is billableParty and patientPaymentCategory is selfFundedPrepayment, with prepaymentDetail full (RVG estimate via feeFor) or split (deposit). The office clicks Raise pre-procedure invoice, which creates the invoice, case and Xero ACCREC plus draft ACCPAY to the anaesthetist at once. The post-authorisation run bills the BTM-based balance net of a visible deduction line. No holding account, transfer, credit note, refund, approval step or letter.

Run nets the prepayment and automatically bills a BTM balance instead of leaving the Procedure off and transferring the prepaid amount

items.title: Prepayment

items.summary: Prepaid Contracts, the Prepaid step-rail path and the typed 'Prepaid · Fixed price' exist, but the payer is one per Booking, and the seeded and built 'split' deposit invoices an agreed $800 rather than the Procedure's price when the invoice is raised.
items.requirement_says: The office makes a Procedure prepaid by choosing Patient > Prepaid on the step rail and a prepaid Contract. A prepaid Contract bills the Procedure's payer, is priced at a fixed price above zero or an office-typed amount (never RVG), and the prepaid amount is the Procedure's price when the prepayment invoice is raised.
items.prototype_does: The rail offers Patient > Standard or Prepaid and lists prepaid Contracts. contractRefusal forces a prepaid Contract to bill the payer, to use a non-RVG pricing kind and to price above zero. The system fallback 'Prepaid · Fixed price' lets the office type an amount. A 'full' prepayment invoices feeFor on the Contract. A Procedure can also carry prepaymentDetail {type:'split', depositAmount}, and the seeded S4 Fri 24 Annette Riley Booking uses an $800 deposit against a $1,200 Contract price. The invoice builder invoices that flat deposit as 'Pre-payment deposit'. The payer comes from Booking.payer, not from each Procedure.
missing_or_wrong: Payer is held on the Booking, not on each Procedure (Donald, 17 Nov, OQ-140), so a prepaid Procedure cannot bill a different payer from its siblings.

Prepayment can be an agreed split deposit (prepaymentDetail split/depositAmount, seeded $800 on a $1,200 price) instead of always the Procedure's price when raised. This is wrong against the current text.
OfficeBillingSetup shows 'Required · $800 seeded' for the split deposit rather than the Contract price.
Minor: procedureRequiresPrepayment and the code comments still say 'INTERIM until Phase 27', so the prepaid trigger is an older reading marked as provisional.

items.summary: Prepayment invoices do use the normal case and Xero pair path, but the payable credits the anaesthetist, whereas the requirement says it credits the AA Holding account.

items.prototype_does: raisePreProcedureInvoice raises an Invoice of kind prePayment plus a BillingCase, then handoffCasesForBooking creates an ACCREC and a draft ACCPAY whose payee is the List's anaesthetist (refuses noAnaesthetist if none). items.summary: No AA Holding account, no cancellation reversal, and the prototype releases a paid prepayment to the List's anaesthetist before the procedure and bills a balance after it, the opposite of the feature's text.
items.requirement_says: Prepayment money is credited to a payables account (the AA Holding account, within trust accounting), not the anaesthetist, and transferred automatically to whoever did the procedure once the List is authorised. Cancelling reverses the prepayment automatically (credit note if unpaid, full refund from holding if paid, credit linked to the original invoice, a later payment sent back). A moved prepaid Booking keeps its price and nothing is recalculated. Nothing further is raised after a prepaid procedure.
items.prototype_does: raisePreProcedureInvoice creates a prePayment invoice for the patient, handoff creates an ACCREC plus ACCPAY payable to the List's anaesthetist, and a received payment releases that payable to them (paymentActions.ts:99). cancelBooking only stamps booking.cancellation. At AUTHORISED the billing run builds a balance invoice with a 'Less pre-payment deposit already invoiced' line. A move repoints nothing, so the payable stays with the original anaesthetist and the final figure is recalculated. The unpaid prepayment is only a warning.

Missing: no payments out of the holding account except by the system

items.summary: Per-Procedure detection from a prepaid Contract satisfies all three acceptance criteria, but the description's per-payer invoicing of Procedures with different payers cannot happen because the payer is one per Booking (OQ-73 and OQ-140 unresolved).
items.requirement_says: A Procedure needs prepayment whenever its Contract is prepaid, and the Booking does if any Procedure does. Only the prepaid Procedure is flagged. Prepaid Procedures that name different payers are invoiced to each payer separately.

The warning is derived from the Booking's prepaymentStatus. Procedures on non-prepaid Contracts are never flagged. buildPrePaymentInvoiceForBooking only picks up the prepaid Procedures. Every prepaid Procedure shares Booking.payer, so there is no different-payer case.
missing_or_wrong: No per-Procedure payer, so 'prepaid Procedures that name different payers are invoiced to each payer separately' cannot occur (depends on US-11.2.2).
The warning is Booking-level text ('Prepayment required. No prepayment invoice has been raised yet.'). It does not name the Procedure or the payer that needs prepayment.
items.verify_note: I checked each acceptance criterion against the selectors and the builder, and all three are met in code. Validation only requires a deposit above zero on a split.

Full amount is an RVG-based estimate, not a Contract price range

items.summary: The office raises the prepayment invoice itself and it is sent at once, with no admin approval step or switch-off setting. The pair's payable goes to the anaesthetist rather than the AA Holding account, only one invoice per Booking is built, the amount can be a split deposit, and the payer lock covers the whole Booking.
items.requirement_says: An admin approves the prepayment invoice on the outgoing-invoices approval screen, and AA can switch the approval off. The system generates and sends it with a prepayment letter. There is one invoice per payer, for the Procedures' price when raised, addressed to their payer. The pair is a receivable from the payer and a payable to the AA Holding account, plus a Xero draft pair. The payer is locked once their own invoice is raised. A later List submit does not invoice it again.
items.prototype_does: raisePreProcedureInvoice is office-only. It builds the Invoice (kind prePayment) and materialises it with send:true at once. handoffCasesForBooking then creates an ACCREC from the payer and an ACCPAY whose payee is the anaesthetist's Xero contact, with amountPayable equal to invoice.total. There is no approval queue and no approval-off setting; the code comment says Phase 27 will do this. Counterparty comes from Booking.payer, so there is one invoice per Booking. 'split' prepayments invoice a flat deposit line. setBookingPayer refuses any payer change once any prepayment invoice exists for the Booking. The raise is refused once the List is AUTHORISED or billed, and 'alreadyRaised' makes it idempotent per Booking. The balance run nets the prepayment. InvoiceDocument shows prepayment wording. There is no prepayment letter.
missing_or_wrong: No admin approval step on the outgoing-invoices approval screen. The office raises and the invoice is sent immediately (send:true).
No setting to switch the approval off (US-13.7.4).
The pair's payable goes to the anaesthetist, not the AA Holding account (the wrong behaviour; the current text says the opposite).
No one-invoice-per-payer grouping across Procedures with different payers, because the payer is per Booking.
The payer lock is whole-Booking, not per payer; 'a payer whose own invoice is not yet raised can still be changed' cannot occur.
The amount may be a split deposit instead of always the Procedures' price when raised.
No prepayment letter is sent with the invoice (US-06.3.6).
The invoice is not generated automatically when the prepaid Contract is picked; it needs the office to click the button.
Idempotence is per Booking, not per payer or Procedure, so a Procedure added after raising cannot get its own prepayment invoice.
evidence: aa-prototype/src/store/xeroHandoff.ts:258-296 (ACCPAY payee is the anaesthetist; amountPayable = invoice.total)

items.summary: There is no AA Holding account anywhere. A paid prepayment's payable is released to the anaesthetist as soon as the money is received, which is the opposite of holding it until the procedure is done.
items.requirement_says: A prepayment is credited to the AA Holding account, a payables sub-ledger creditor beside the anaesthetists that is never paid. The prepayment invoice's pair is a receivable from the payer and a payable to the holding account. Its balance is the deposits received for procedures not yet done. Nothing is paid to the anaesthetist before the procedure. Money leaves only by a system-raised transfer to the anaesthetist who did the List, after authorisation, or by a refund.
items.prototype_does: The prepayment ACCREC/ACCPAY pair is created like an ordinary invoice. The ACCPAY payee is the anaesthetist, and once payment is received payableReleasedFor releases the payable to the anaesthetist for the amount received. The seeded paid prepayment INV0001 is already disbursed. There is no holding creditor, balance, transfer pair, refund path or admin view. Comments in listMoveActions.ts and slotActions.ts mention 'the AA Holding account' as a later phase only.
missing_or_wrong: No AA Holding account entity or balance (single creditor) in the ledger, Xero simulator or admin.
The prepayment pair's payable goes to the anaesthetist, not the holding account, and is released on payment rather than after the procedure.
No second transfer pair from the holding account to the anaesthetist who did the List when the office authorises it (OQ-125).
Nothing enforces that money leaves the holding account only by system transfer or refund, and nothing shows a balance of deposits for procedures not yet done.
No refund-from-holding path (US-06.5.2) and no repointing on a move to another anaesthetist (US-06.5.4); the 'Phase 41 seam' comments mark this.
evidence: aa-prototype/src/domain/billing/payableRelease.ts:1-40 (payment releases payable to the amount received)
aa-prototype/src/domain/seed/billing.ts (seeded prepayment paid and disbursed to the payee)
searched: AA Holding|holding account|prepayHolding|holdingAccount in aa-prototype/src -> only comments (store/listMoveActions.ts:163,375,445; store/slotActions.ts:448)

Add a Xero-simulator button 'Simulate prepayment received' that shows the credit landing in the holding account with nothing released to the anaesthetist. On the Booking after List authorisation, show a 'Transfer prepayment to anaesthetist' step (or run it automatically on authorise) that shows the second journal pair.

The prototype implements the earlier 'anaesthetist paid when the money arrives' reading, which the 10 November note says to change, so Contradicts is right and Missing would be wrong.

items.summary: Cancelling a prepaid Booking only soft-cancels it; no credit note or refund is raised and there is no holding account.
items.requirement_says: Cancelling a Booking with an unpaid prepayment automatically raises a credit note; with a paid prepayment the full amount is refunded from the AA Holding account, recorded as a credit reversing the receivable and the holding payable; a payment after the credit note is refunded.
items.prototype_does: cancelBooking marks the Booking cancelled with a reason and excludes it from billing, validation and the prepayment flag. The prepayment invoice, its case and its ACCPAY are left untouched; nothing is credited or refunded.
missing_or_wrong: No automatic credit note for an unpaid prepayment
No full refund for a paid prepayment
No ledger reversal linked to the original invoice
No handling of a later payment after the credit
The orphaned invoice and ACCPAY remain live in Xero after cancel

items.summary: A rebooked new Booking does start its own prepayment, but at an estimated fee rather than the new anaesthetist's fixed price, and the original is never credited or refunded.

items.summary: A move leaves the prepayment untouched and bills nothing again, but the existing payable stays with the original anaesthetist and there is no holding account, so the new anaesthetist is not paid from the prepayment.

No patient email.

No second-step transfer to the new anaesthetist
No optional patient email
Not-billed-again and no-recalculation ACs do hold

items.summary: Office review is largely built, but the payer is one BookingPayer on the Booking, not on each Procedure, so the per-Procedure 'Paid by' payer and per-Procedure child warning (changed 17 Nov, OQ-140) are contradicted; OQ-135 is open and the prototype takes option 1 (no flag).
items.requirement_says: Admin reviews each submitted Booking: per Procedure the text received, Contract and RVG code, insurer and approval number, each Procedure's payer in its 'Paid by' line (patient by default, changeable to a parent or guardian, only where the Contract bills the payer), flags for a changed Contract, a typed price beside the computed one and a Contract no longer fitting the List, Needs an invoice destination and Needs a price. A mild non-blocking child-payer warning appears on each Procedure billed to the payer (two Procedures give two warnings), and the admin can still approve.

The payer is one BookingPayer on the Booking: Review's PayerAndInsurer shows one 'Patient pays' or 'Payer: name' per Booking with a Change link to the Admin Booking. The Billing card's 'Paid by' line (PaidByRow) shows the invoiced party or a fee split with a Split action, not an editable payer. The child-payer warning is derived once per Booking (childPayerOn takes booking.payer) and yields one warning naming the patient. A Disabled Contract raises no flag (D81, matching OQ-135 option 1). Flags never block.
missing_or_wrong: CONTRADICTS: the payer is stored on the Booking (Booking.payer, types.ts:811-812; BookingPayer type, types.ts:237-258, whose own comment says 'one payer per Booking'; setBookingPayer in store/payerActions.ts), not on each Procedure, so one Booking cannot have two Procedures billed to different payers, which the story now states

CONTRADICTS: the child-payer warning is derived once per Booking (childPayerOn in domain/billing/whoIsBilled.ts:229-239 takes booking.payer; rules/childPayer.ts:21-27 returns a single warning), where the acceptance criterion wants one warning per Procedure billed to the payer, so two child-payer Procedures show two warnings

Review shows the payer in a per-Booking PayerAndInsurer cell (ReviewScreen.tsx:363, :569-585) rather than in each Procedure's 'Paid by' line, and its Change opens the Booking, not a per-Procedure change

The 'Paid by' line (PaidByRow.tsx) is the invoiced party or fee split with a Split action; there is no 'change the payer to a guardian' action per Procedure, and the 'Under 18' and contact warnings sit in the Booking-level payer view rather than the Procedure's line
The 'change offered to the other Procedures that bill the same payer, ticked' behaviour (US-11.2.2, reached from Review's change) does not exist
No seed Booking has two Procedures billed to payers that each leave a child as payer (payerReviewBookings.ts has one child-payer Booking, Ella Moana)
payerContactMissing is evaluated per Booking (BookingDetailBody.tsx:632) and would need to follow the payer per Procedure

OQ-135 is open: no flag for a Disabled Contract on an open Procedure. The prototype's no-flag default is consistent with the text as written and is a one-rule addition to REVIEW_FLAG_RULES if answered 'flag'. This is not a contradiction.
evidence: aa-prototype/src/apps/admin/screens/ReviewScreen.tsx:363, :569-585 (PayerAndInsurer per Booking; Change opens the Booking), :373 (ProcedureStack per Procedure)
items.verify_note: Re-read US-07.2.2, OQ-135, OQ-140 and US-11.2.2, then re-opened the code. Confirmed payer is on Booking (types.ts), childPayerOn and the childPayer rule are per Booking, and Review's PayerAndInsurer is per Booking. Contradicts, not Partial, because implemented behaviour is wrong against the 17 Nov reading (per-Procedure payer, per-Procedure warnings, change offered to the other Procedures). The review flags, insurer and approval-number warning, flagged-for-office alert and Needs an invoice destination and Needs a price flags are present, so the rest of the story is met. The reviewer's size L, surfaces and empty demo_trigger are sound. I added one missed point, the 'change offered to the other Procedures' behaviour. Note that US-11.2.2 and OQ-140 are themselves still open (AA to confirm), so the contradiction is against a provisional ruling.

items.summary: The ACCREC + DRAFT ACCPAY pair, ID storage, InvoiceNumber and Reference are implemented, but a prepayment invoice's ACCPAY is raised to the anaesthetist rather than the AA Holding account, which contradicts the story's parenthetical.
items.requirement_says: Per ledger pair the engine creates an ACCREC to the billable party and a DRAFT ACCPAY to the anaesthetist (for a prepayment invoice, to the AA Holding account) in one transaction and stores both Xero IDs on the ledger record; each carries the engine's unique invoice number as InvoiceNumber and the case reference as Reference.
items.prototype_does: handoffCase creates the ACCREC and a draft ACCPAY in one mutate, stores accRecId/accPayId on the BillingCase, puts the engine invoice number in InvoiceNumber and the case reference in Reference; the fault path creates no half pair. The ACCPAY's InvoiceNumber is the engine number with a '-P' suffix. Prepayment pre-invoices (raisePrePayment) call the same handoffCasesForBooking, so the ACCPAY payee is always the anaesthetist contact; there is no AA Holding account contact, payee or ledger anywhere in the code (only comments in listMoveActions.ts and slotActions.ts and a test comment assume one).
missing_or_wrong: Prepayment ACCPAY pays the anaesthetist (the List's anaesthetist) instead of the AA Holding account (WRONG behaviour: payee chosen by anaesthetistContactSpec regardless of prepayment).

No AA Holding account contact or payee in the Xero sim, so the prepayment pair cannot show the holding-account payable, and no later second (settlement) pair exists. Overlaps US-09.1.3 (Agreed) and EP-06 (US-06.5.1, US-06.4.1).

The ACCPAY's InvoiceNumber is '<engine number>-P', not the engine's own number as the story's wording says every invoice in the pair carries; reviewer missed this. Minor, and arguably a deliberate Xero-uniqueness workaround, but the ACCPAY should be checked against the wording or the story clarified.
Draft versus approved bill question (Greg 10 Nov) is not surfaced in the sim; it is an open design point, low weight.

items.summary: Simulated Xero payment webhook matched by stored accRecId, authorising the ACCPAY for the full or exact amount received (min(received, payable)), idempotent, with demo triggers.

items.summary: The prototype records disbursement, but as an AA office action (Admin 'Run payables', and a Xero-simulator button that calls the same office function), not as the engine detecting an ACCPAY paid in Xero's payables run via webhook or poll; this is the older reading that OQ-111 (answered 4 Nov, not yet seen by Greg) now reverses. Story is Verify, so graded against the text as written.
items.requirement_says: Xero makes the payment to the anaesthetist in its payables run; the engine learns of it by webhook or the daily poll and records the disbursement against the ledger payable, so paid-into-AA and disbursed-to-anaesthetist stay two separately tracked states. The system tracks payments, it does not make them.
items.prototype_does: Both paths call the system's own disbursement writer. (1) Admin Billing monitor 'Run payables' card (unbadged product UI, office-only): copy says 'N payables authorised, $X to disburse to anaesthetists'; pays amountAuthorised minus amountDisbursed on every ACCPAY, writing Disbursement rows with a payablesRunId, accPay.amountDisbursed/status paid, and BillingCase disbursedAmount/status 'disbursed' (audited xero.disbursed, actor 'Payables run'). (2) The Xero simulator pair-detail button 'Simulate payment and payout' / 'Pay <anaesthetist> now' applies the customer payment via receivePayment (source webhook), then calls disbursePayable with OFFICE_ACTOR, so the Xero-side payout is just the office function. The two-state split itself exists (receivedAmount vs disbursedAmount; chips in InvoiceDocument, Billing monitor, Web accounts). Webhook and poll machinery exists only for ACCREC payments; there is no ACCPAY-paid event, no Xero-side 'paid' state separate from the engine's record, and the daily poll does not detect payable payments.
missing_or_wrong: WRONG: Admin 'Run payables' button and card copy make the system perform the disbursement ('to disburse to anaesthetists'), contradicting OQ-111 (Xero pays, system only tracks)
WRONG: disbursement is written by an office-role action (disbursePayable/runPayables refuse non-office actors) rather than by an engine detection handler fed by Xero
MISSING: no ACCPAY payment detection by webhook (a receipt-like handler for a paid ACCPAY with idempotency key and source webhook|poll)
MISSING: the reconciliation poll (runReconciliationPoll) only re-detects ACCREC PaymentIn records; it does not catch a missed ACCPAY payment

MISSING: Xero simulator has no 'Pay in payables run' action that marks the ACCPAY paid in Xero itself, separate from the engine's amountDisbursed; Xero and engine share one XeroAccPay record so 'detected' is not distinguishable from 'made'
MISSING: no visible state where Xero has paid but the engine has not yet recorded it (e.g. missed webhook) and no way to show the poll catching it

No field, state or screen models a hospital paying the anaesthetist or a remittance advice being reconciled. BillingRoute (hospital|billableParty|insurer) says who is invoiced, not where payment goes. Insurer.acceptsDirectClaims means AA bills the insurer directly, not payment direct to the anaesthetist. 'Remittance' appears only as the InvoiceNumber matching-key copy in DemoXero.

The Xero 'remittance' copy is only the matching key, a distinct topic. Confidence stays medium only because the item is Proposed and its two stories (US-10.1.1, US-10.1.2) were not separately graded.

items.summary: Payable release on receipt is built correctly, but the prototype makes the anaesthetist payment itself (office 'Run payables' button, Xero-sim 'Pay <anaesthetist> now'), whereas FT-10.2 and OQ-111 (answered 4 Nov) say Xero's payables run makes the payment and the system only detects and records it.
items.requirement_says: Once a receivable is paid, its matching payable is authorised for the next payables run, so the anaesthetist is paid only what AA has received. The payment is made in Xero's payables run; the system records and tracks it (US-09.2.4) and does not make the payment itself (OQ-111).
items.prototype_does: receivePayment authorises the DRAFT ACCPAY for exactly the cumulative amount received (DRAFT to AUTHORISED). The admin Billing monitor has an unbadged 'Run payables' card and button (runPayables) that disburses authorised minus disbursed, writes a Disbursement and marks the case Disbursed, as system actor 'Payables run'; the source comment calls it product UI, not a simulation. The Xero sim's PairDetail has 'Simulate payment and payout' / 'Pay <anaesthetist> now', which calls receivePayment then disbursePayable(OFFICE_ACTOR). Nothing detects a disbursement made in Xero (reconciliationPoll and the webhook path handle ACCREC receipts only; no ACCPAY-paid event). No weekly cycle, ISO week, close or payment day anywhere.
missing_or_wrong: WRONG: the payment to the anaesthetist is made by the system (Admin 'Run payables' and Xero-sim 'Pay now' both call store disbursement actions, audited as a system/office action); the requirement says Xero's payables run makes it and the engine detects and records it
The payables run is unbadged product UI in Admin, not a Xero action; no 'Xero payables run' simulation followed by webhook/poll detection of the ACCPAY payment (the US-09.2.4 side)

No payment-cycle notion (ISO week, Friday close, Monday reconciliation, payment day); the cycle is Proposed and OQ-47 is open (Greg's latest: Monday to Sunday week, Thursday payment), so this is a note to track rather than a hard gap
Release rule itself (authorise exactly the cumulative amount received, remainder stays on the receivable) is correct and matches
evidence: aa-prototype/src/store/payablesActions.ts:1-10,19,56-140,147-169 (runPayables/disbursePayable disburse as 'Payables run' system actor; header says unbadged office action, not a simulation)
aa-prototype/src/store/index.ts:303-304 (only two callers of the disbursement actions: BillingMonitorScreen and DemoXero)
searched: ISO week|payment cycle|weekly|Friday in src -> none; reconciliationPoll.ts has no payable/disburs handling
items.demo_trigger: Re-home the payout as a Xero simulation: on /admin/billing and /demo/xero a badged (Demo simulation) button 'Run Xero payables run' that pays every authorised ACCPAY in the simulated Xero and then fires the payment webhook (plus the existing 'Run reconciliation poll' as catch-up for a missed one) so the engine records the Disbursement; the Billing monitor 'Run payables' card becomes read-only tracking ('Awaiting Xero payables run: n payables, $x'). Optionally show the current ISO payment week beside it once OQ-47 settles.
items.verify_note: Re-read FT-10.2, OQ-111 (answered 4 Nov: Xero makes the payment, system tracks it) and OQ-47, then the code. Confirmed runPayables and disbursePayable have only two callers (Billing monitor button and Xero-sim button), both making the payment in-system, and no ACCPAY-payment detection exists in reconciliationPoll or paymentActions. Contradicts is right (implemented behaviour is wrong, not merely absent). Release rule is correct. Demo-guide lines 03-demo-script.md ~528 and ~652-655, 02-workflows Workflow 7 step 6 would change.

items.prototype_does: runMonthlyFeeInvoices raises one kind 'aaFee' ACCREC (no ACCPAY) for every active anaesthetist without an invoice for the month, including zero-BCTI ones; BCTIs counted paid-only, once, against the procedure's anaesthetist; recordAaFeePayment pays it into AA's own account with no receipt and no payable; nothing deducts it from payables; web Accounts > AA fees shows the anaesthetist's invoices.

items.title: AA fee invoicing

items.summary: Every procedure follows one route: payer pays AA (ACCREC), AA disburses to the anaesthetist (ACCPAY); no direct pathway exists. The trust-account point from the 10 Nov accountant meeting is a Note (not a rule or AC) and is not labelled, which is a minor wording gap only.
items.requirement_says: The system models exactly one payment path for every procedure: the billable party pays AA, and AA disburses to the anaesthetist. (Note: all receipts go through the one trust account.)
items.prototype_does: Every invoiced Booking gets an ACCREC paired with a DRAFT ACCPAY; payments are applied only to the ACCREC and the anaesthetist is paid only via the ACCPAY. Xero sim cards read 'ACCREC · MONEY INTO AA' and 'ACCPAY · MONEY OUT OF AA'; the invoice document shows 'Paid into AA account' and 'Disbursed to anaesthetist'. No direct-pay or remittance-to-anaesthetist path. No prototype text anywhere names a trust account or a separate Holding account.
evidence: aa-prototype/src/store/paymentActions.ts:1-26,96-100 (payments land on the ACCREC, payable follows)
aa-prototype/src/store/xeroHandoff.ts (ACCREC + DRAFT ACCPAY pair per case)

items.verify_note: Status is Proposed. The story body states only the one-route rule and has no acceptance criteria; the trust-account sentence sits under Notes. Prepayments are not modelled to a Holding account, but that is a US-08.3.x gap, not this story's. Low risk that a presenter would want a 'one trust account' label; optional wording, not a gap.
items.title: All payments into AA

items.title: Two payment states

items.summary: A payment authorises the matching ACCPAY for exactly the cumulative amount received; a part payment releases only that amount with the remainder outstanding on the receivable; authorised payables are what the (in-system) run picks up. OQ-47 (weekly cycle, BCTI approval) is open but does not change this story's rule.
items.requirement_says: When a receivable is paid, the matching payable is authorised so it enters the next payables run. Paid in full releases the whole payable; a part payment releases a payable for exactly the amount received and the remainder stays outstanding on the receivable.
items.prototype_does: receivePayment clamps to the balance, bumps ACCREC amountReceived and status, and sets ACCPAY amountAuthorised to payableReleasedFor(newReceived, payable) (min of cumulative received and payable), flipping DRAFT to AUTHORISED on first release; a second payment lifts the cumulative figure. Idempotent by key (webhook or poll). payablesDue counts authorised minus disbursed; the Billing monitor says 'A payable authorises for exactly what its ACCREC has received'. Demo triggers 'Payment received full/half/replay' on invoice and Xero pair pages cover it, and the S4 script proves it with two runs across a part-then-balance payment.
items.demo_trigger: Existing: Demo actions > 'Payment received · full' and 'Payment received · half' on /admin/invoices/:invoiceId and /demo/xero/invoices/:accRecId.
items.verify_note: Status Agreed, so re-checked closely. Story has no acceptance criteria beyond the two rule paragraphs; both hold in paymentActions.ts and payableRelease.ts (cumulative, exact to the cent, remainder left on ACCREC). The story links to the weekly 'payables run' (US-10.2.7), which is unbuilt, and the run itself is made in-system (the FT-10.2 contradiction); both are graded under FT-10.2 and US-10.2.7, not here, because this story's rule is only the authorisation. Kept Matches.
items.title: Payable released to match the amount received

items.summary: Every receipt (webhook or poll) is reconciled to its billing case/invoice and displayed against the invoice; poll catches missed webhooks.
items.requirement_says: Every receipt recorded in Xero is reconciled back to the ledger record it belongs to, keeping the internal ledger (system of record) in step with Xero.
items.prototype_does: receivePayment (shared by webhook and poll, idempotent by key) writes PaymentIn, updates ACCREC, BillingCase and a BillingReceipt keyed to case/ACCREC; runReconciliationPoll on dayAdvanced re-detects unmirrored Xero payments and applies them via the same handler with the original receipt date. Web Payments shows receipt against invoice number; Xero pair shows engine link.
items.demo_trigger: Existing: Control panel 'Run reconciliation poll' and day advance catch the seeded missed-webhook payment.
items.verify_note: Confirmed Status: Confirmed item; re-read poll and receivePayment. 'Ledger as system of record' (US-08.3.2) is an EP-08 gap; here the BillingCase mirror stands in. Confidence stays medium for that reason.
items.title: Reconcile back to the ledger

items.summary: The prototype has no bulk-payment or bank-reconciliation representation: the Xero simulator pays one invoice at a time and has no reconciliation or unmatched-items view, so the boundary (Xero's add-on matches bulk remittances; leftovers stay in Xero for the office) is not shown. Not OutOfScope because a simulator view can make it presenter-explainable.
items.requirement_says: Bulk hospital payments covering multiple invoices are matched by Xero's own bank reconciliation and remittance add-on, not the Billing/Invoice Engine; any item the add-on cannot match stays as an unmatched item in Xero's bank reconciliation for the office to handle there.
items.prototype_does: Nothing that shows it. Payments reach the engine only as single-invoice webhook or poll events (full or half). The only related text is Xero-sim copy that the engine's InvoiceNumber is the key hospitals and insurers quote on remittances so remittance matching can key on it. Xero sim has Contacts and Invoices tabs only. The engine does no bulk matching (consistent with the requirement), but nothing shows Xero doing it or the unmatched leftovers.
missing_or_wrong: No simulated bank feed or Xero bank reconciliation view
No bulk payment covering several invoices (one bank line, several ACCRECs) that Xero's add-on matches by reference and amount before the engine sees it
No unmatched line left in Xero for the office, and no 'what to do' hint for a receipt with no reference

Optional second button 'Office matches line'.

items.prototype_does: domain/nhi.ts validateNhi detects format by character class, checks current format by weighted mod 11 (the real Health NZ algorithm; RFP's own example ZAA0067 only validates under mod 11) and new format by mod 23, rejects I and O, gives plain reasons; generateNhi makes non-sequential seeded NHIs of both formats. Integrations Validators tab shows an NHI validator and says on screen that the RFP's 'Modulus 24' label does not fit its own examples.
items.demo_trigger: Existing: Admin, Integrations, Validators tab accepts ZAA0067 / ACA31FM and rejects a bad check digit.
items.verify_note: Read nhi.ts algorithms. Catalogue literally says modulus 24 for the current format but the prototype uses mod 11 by prior ruling and flags it on screen; behaviour a presenter shows (both formats validated, bad check rejected) satisfies the story, so kept Matches with medium confidence. If the catalogue wording is ever treated as binding this would become Contradicts, but switching to mod 24 would reject real NHIs.

items.summary: One routine runs registered rules and raises several warnings per Booking, each with kind, strength and text, and none blocks. The child-payer warning is raised once per Booking, where the story and its acceptance criterion now want it on each Procedure billed to the payer with one to-do per Booking. The patient-balance warning is missing entirely.
items.requirement_says: One standard routine raises a warning for each condition found on a Booking or its billable parties, each with its own text and several per Booking. Kinds are before-procedure and after-procedure, strengths are mild and strong, and a warning never blocks. The current warnings are: unpaid prepayment; billable patient with a balance (owing mild under the alert threshold and strong over it, days counted from the invoice date, credit balance mild); child left as a Procedure's payer (mild, shown on each Procedure billed to the payer, one to-do per Booking); base units outside the RVG range (after-procedure, office); and insured Booking with no approval number (shown to the office and the anaesthetist). An insurer Booking with no insurer Contract raises no warning.
items.prototype_does: evaluateWarnings runs five registered rules (prepaymentUnpaid, baseUnitsOutsideGuide, childPayer, approvalNumberMissing, splitDoesNotFit) over WarningFacts and returns several warnings sorted strong first. Each carries kind, strength and text, and nothing in lifecycle or authorise reads them, so they never block. prepaymentUnpaid is before-procedure and strong. baseUnitsOutsideGuide is after-procedure and mild, one per Procedure, skipping additional Procedures. approvalNumberMissing is before-procedure and mild, and a missing insurer Contract raises nothing. The office can clear a warning, and the anaesthetist sees them in the panel. childPayer returns one finding with no procedureId, so there is one warning key per Booking, and childPayerOn tests the Booking's payer, the patient's age and whether any Procedure bills the payer. There is no balance rule: the only trace is a boolean outstandingPriorBalance flag on the Billing monitor row, and the demo-trigger text in the registry says a balance sample is a later rule.
missing_or_wrong: Child-payer warning is per Booking, not per Procedure billed to the payer. childPayer.ts:20-25 returns a single finding with no procedureId and the key has no procedure part. The story (Donald, 17 November) and acceptance criterion 'Child warning per Procedure' want one warning on each such Procedure, with one dashboard to-do per Booking. This is the older reading. The change needs per-Procedure evaluation, per-Procedure keys, Procedure-level display and openWarnings collapsing to one child row per Booking. OQ-140 (AA to confirm) is open and also questions a payer per Procedure.

Patient-balance warning is missing. There is no rule, no WarningRuleId, no per-patient balance or invoice-age fact, no alert threshold (fixed 90 days until US-13.7.4), no mild-under or strong-over escalation counted from the invoice date, and no mild credit-balance warning. Searched balance|owing across src with no rule found. outstandingPriorBalance is a yes or no flag that is not a warning, has no strength, and does not reach the to-do list or the anaesthetist's Booking.
The routine reads only the Booking's own facts (payer, funder, Procedures). It has no billable-party fact, which the balance check needs.
splitDoesNotFit is a registered rule that the story's list does not name. It is harmless but extra.
Unpaid prepayment is always strong, with no date-driven strength. The story leaves strength 'not yet set', so this is a provisional reading and not a defect.
evidence: aa-prototype/src/domain/warnings/routine.ts:35-58 (evaluateWarnings: several per Booking, keyed by booking, rule and finding.procedureId)
aa-prototype/src/shared/demoTriggers/registry.ts:1197 (raise-sample-warnings text says 'Later rules add... a paying patient with a balance')
searched: balance|owing in aa-prototype/src (non-test) with no warning rule or threshold found
items.demo_trigger: Extend the existing 'Raise sample warnings' Demo action (Admin Day, Booking detail and Mobile Booking, backed by store/warningSamples.ts) to also stage patient-balance samples: an invoice dated 40 days ago (mild), one dated 120 days ago (strong), and a credit balance (mild). Also make its child-payer sample put one warning on each of two Procedures billed to the payer, with one to-do row for the Booking. 'Clear sample warnings' already reverses them.
items.verify_note: I re-opened routine.ts, the rule registry, WarningFacts, childPayer.ts, childPayerOn, and the baseUnits, approval and prepayment rules. I searched for balance and owing across the source. I confirmed the child warning is one finding per Booking, which the story's AC 'Child warning per Procedure' now contradicts, and that the patient-balance rule does not exist (the registry text itself calls it a later rule). Contradicts stands over Partial because implemented behaviour (per-Booking child warning) is wrong against the current text. The prototype keeps the payer at Booking level, and OQ-140 may change that. The per-Procedure child warning can still be driven from each Procedure's Contract billsTo, so the gap is closeable without waiting on OQ-140. Size M is reasonable: a new rule with seeded balance facts, plus re-keying the child warning and its display. Surfaces and demo trigger are sound.

items.requirement_says: St George's and Southern Cross (OQ-109) are integrated today and the first release syncs both into the matching screen (FT-02.1). More feeds, automatic matching, HL7 v2 and FHIR are Future Work; the NHI lookup is in scope as a simple API. Transport is an adapter over one queue/retry/translation path, with a maintained per-hospital matrix (v2 or FHIR, polled or pushed).
items.prototype_does: Simulated integration tier: canned HL7 v2 and FHIR R4 messages from three feeds (St George's HL7, Christchurch Public HL7 misconfigured on purpose, Southern Cross FHIR) are stored, deduped, retried 3 times then dead-lettered or parked, and applied directly as Bookings onto an existing ACTIVE List of Dr Souter. The Admin Integrations Messages and Feed config tabs and the simulator page are badged Future scope, with a note that the in-scope path is a download into a matching screen. The NHI Look up in the manual booking form uses canned records. There is no matching screen and no hospital download intake; the only trace is a 'hospitalRow' draft origin type and a 'Hospital download' source label stamped by the interim HL7 create path.
missing_or_wrong: No matching screen or review-and-merge intake for hospital downloads (FT-02.1, US-02.1.5). Hospital messages bypass it and write Bookings straight onto a List; integrationActions.ts:149,169 label this interim until Phase 33. DraftListsScreen has no hospital-row or matching content.
The first-release automatic sync of the two integrated hospitals is not shown as in-scope intake. The only HL7/FHIR UI is badged Future and used as the S1 path.
Which two hospitals are integrated is unresolved (OQ-109, St George's and Southern Cross vs Forte). Prototype feeds are St George's, Christchurch Public and Southern Cross.
No transport-adapter concept or per-hospital configuration matrix: the Feed config tab shows only transport (HL7 v2 or FHIR) and field mapping, with no polled vs pushed attribute or adapter switch.
Message routing is hardcoded to Dr Souter's 28/30 July Lists; an incoming booking is not matched to a List or anaesthetist.
The NHI lookup is canned and shown in the manual booking form only. It is not framed as a national-service API call from the integration tier (minor, adequate for demo).

summary_md:
### Headline

The prototype is the July RFP model with Phases 15 to 32 layered on. Calendar, Slots, Lists, Draft Lists, pairings, tiers, warnings engine, the AA fee run and the Xero simulation are close to the catalogue. Money and intake are not. Of roughly 235 graded items, about 40 Match, about 25 are Partial, about 15 are Missing, and the rest are Contradicts or Grouping. Contradicts dominates EP-02 to EP-08, EP-11 and EP-12: the prototype implements a different, superseded design there, not a smaller version of the new one. EP-01, EP-10 and most of EP-13 are near done. The core is one coordinated rework: Contract (holder, dated versions, lines, flags) replaces billing route plus Type 1/2/3. Pricing, completion, prepayment, invoicing, payer, review and events all hang off it. Statuses were not used to scope work; they appear below only where an open question (OQ) makes a gap unsafe.

### Themes

**1. Contract-centred billing (XL).** Billing route, optional governing Contract, Type 1/2/3 and protected default Type 1s go. In: holders with an is-billed flag, dated Contract versions with AA code, standalone lines, one AA-held No contract (RVG), mandatory Contract per Procedure, staged review and submit, authorisation snapshot, filtered picker, anaesthetist may change Contract until AUTHORISED. Items: EP-04, FT-04.1 to 04.3, US-04.1.1 to 04.1.6, US-04.2.x, US-04.3.x, FT-03.4, US-03.4.1, US-08.1.1, US-07.3.1. DM-07, DM-09, DM-10, DM-48, DM-49, DM-57, DM-08, DM-16. RV-06, RV-11, RV-18, RV-32. Split into model and maths, versioning and staging screens, picker and booking setup.

**2. Pricing, units and modifiers (XL).** Price, rate and discount become values on the Procedure; no mandatory reason; Contract flag gates the anaesthetist; $0 gives a no-charge invoice; discount is its own invoice line; modifier units split above four; RVG becomes a hidden-key master (NZSA 2021, duplicate codes); modifiers become records with explanations, age pre-applied, ASA ordinary; out-of-range warns instead of blocking; completion rules reworked ("finish", not "handover"). Items: FT-05.1 to 05.4, US-05.x, FT-03.3, FT-03.5, US-03.3.x, US-03.5.x, US-03.6.1. DM-13, DM-43, DM-44, DM-50, DM-14, DM-15, DM-46. RV-03, RV-04, RV-07 to RV-10, RV-21, RV-22, RV-38. Many S quick wins (NHI, wording, reason removal, make-primary).

**3. Hospital intake matching screen (XL).** Nothing exists: HL7/FHIR and PDF rows apply straight to Bookings. Needed: staged rows, match/create/Draft List/assign/reject, per-row change type, field differences for approval, unmatched queue, day move as cancel plus new, edits allowed until AUTHORISED, third feed (CPH) out of scope. Items: EP-02, FT-02.1, FT-02.5, US-02.1.1/2/4/5, US-02.5.7, US-02.3.1, EP-14 (boundary). DM-34, DM-51. RV-12 to RV-16.

**4. NHI mandatory and source text (M, tied to 3).** Remove provisional patients and "NHI pending"; waiting-for-NHI queue with urgency; text exactly as received per source plus a separate invoice description. Items: US-11.1.1, US-11.1.4, US-11.1.5, US-03.1.5, US-03.1.9, US-08.4.6. DM-30, DM-51. RV-20.

**5. Prepayment and holding account (XL).** Trigger is a prepaid Contract, amount is the line price, admin approval plus letter, payable to a holding account, second pair at authorise, refund on cancel, no automatic balance. Today the anaesthetist is paid before the procedure. Items: EP-06, FT-06.2 to 06.5, US-06.x, FT-08.1, FT-08.3, US-08.2.2, US-08.3.1, FT-09.1, US-09.1.1, US-09.1.3. DM-20, DM-21, DM-22. RV-05, RV-24.

**6. Events, additional invoices, credit notes (XL).** Post-op addendum Booking is replaced by events on the Procedure, additional free-form invoices, credit-in-full-then-rebill, negative payables netted in a weekly cycle. Items: FT-03.7, US-03.7.x, US-05.5.2, FT-08.6, US-08.6.1 to 08.6.5, US-10.2.6. DM-17, DM-18, DM-24, DM-25. RV-23.

**7. Edit window and anaesthetist views (M).** Anaesthetist edits stay open on SUBMITTED; a List leaves the main view at AUTHORISED (not billed); balances show invoices immediately; search by name/NHI/date; scroll back. Items: EP-07, FT-07.2, FT-07.4, US-07.2.1, US-07.2.3, US-07.4.1, US-07.4.2, US-03.1.6, US-03.1.7. DM-55. RV-19.

### Structural first

Screen work built before these lands is rebuilt twice. Suggested order:

1. DM-13 (RVG group, hidden key), DM-48 (holders), then DM-07, DM-09, DM-49 (Contract versions, lines, No contract) in one step with DM-46 (remove BillingLine). Then DM-10 (Procedure picks Contract and line), which unblocks DM-43, DM-44, DM-50, DM-14, DM-15, DM-08 and DM-11.
2. DM-22 (internal ledger with its own payable) before DM-21 (holding account) and DM-20 (prepaid trigger); DM-17 (events) before DM-18, DM-24, then DM-25.
3. DM-30 (NHI required) and DM-51 (source text) before DM-34 (matching rows).
4. DM-57 (staged Contract changes) after DM-07 and DM-09.
5. Independent, can run any time: DM-55, DM-56, DM-42, DM-41, DM-32, DM-12. DM-29 follows DM-22. DM-45 is a policy note, fold into DM-07 or DM-24.

Every seed or type change needs a PERSIST_VERSION bump, canvas-golden and seed tests refreshed. About 26 non-test files read governingContractId or billingRoute, so DM-10 is the widest change.

### Remove or rework (reverse check)

- Remove: attachments on Bookings and Lists (RV-01, M); GST period (RV-02, S); rate x time billing and Method 3 flag (RV-03, M; keep fixed ancillary lines until events exist); ACC "should not bill patient" review flag (RV-37, S).
- Rework (large): prepayment category and split (RV-05), default Type 1 fallback (RV-06), billing-time re-resolution (RV-11), route plus Type model (RV-18), prepaid pair paying anaesthetist (RV-24), addendum Booking (RV-23), HL7 auto-apply and third feed (RV-16).
- Rework (small to medium): price reason and flag (RV-04), ordinal pricing (RV-07), modifier split (RV-08), P1 absorption (RV-09), range hard bound (RV-10), completion rules (RV-21), ASA seeding (RV-22), unavailability conflict (RV-25), notice caption and OQ-84 hint (RV-26), office write-through with no Save (RV-28), per-Procedure payer (RV-30), line-level funder split (RV-31), in-place Contract edits (RV-32), GST receipts (RV-33), ageing buckets (RV-35), prior-balance pill (RV-36), modifier master values (RV-38).
- Hide from demo: Surgeon PDF tab (RV-12, no Future badge), automated change behaviours (RV-13), Productivity and Leave panels (RV-34).
- Keep as scaffold: reliability tooling residue (RV-15), photo capture (RV-17).
- Owner questions, not defects: office single-Booking move targets (RV-27); anaesthetist seeing no price (RV-29, Donald's own 28 Sept decision, conflicts with US-03.1.2 and FT-03.5).

### Demo impact

- S1: Beat 1 (Fire hospital message creates the Booking, "arrives in a later build") rewrites around the matching screen. Beat 3 capture changes: optional numeric RVG codes, no ASA seeding, modifier explanations, "finish" wording, Contract line on screen.
- S2: Beats 1b, 3 and 3a (sickness conflict, assign to closed session) change with OQ-81. Phone-advice beat needs the optional "as given" text and mandatory NHI. Beat 3c (own move) gains single-Booking move. Beat 4 and "submit sheet" copy change with the until-AUTHORISED edit rule; review screen content changes. Notification beat loses busy-morning paging.
- S3: billing Beats 1 to 2 (payer/route wording, pair), split-billing and two-funder beats, payables beat if the prepay payable moves to the holding account, GST and balances messaging (invoices now immediate).
- S4: Beat 1 (prepayment warning, Annette Riley), Beat 2 (post-op addendum, explicitly interim), billing failure and retry (relies on default fallback and un-end-dating), dead-letter and feed-mapping beats (CPH feed).
- Compliance tour: Contract effective-dating beat (edit in place becomes a new dated version), ASA edit seeding units, Master data Contracts click paths. Cheat sheet lines on "default Type 1", billing route, "office-only edits" after submit, and "Prior balance" also need edits.
- Unchanged: FT-02.4 ad hoc add (bar NHI), S2 own-move line "nothing recalculated", most fee-run beats.

### Demo-trigger buttons

The product owner's pattern: screen-contextual buttons in the top control area. Roughly 55 items name a trigger; about half already exist and need repointing (Simulate sickness, Fire hospital message, Stage post-op scenario, Authorise List, Raise sample warnings, month-end fee run). About 25 need genuinely new buttons. Clusters:

dataModelDeltas.title: The payer moves from the Booking to each Procedure: two Procedures on one Booking can bill two different people, grouped into one invoice per payer
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Who is billed is the Contract's own setting (holder Party or payer); that is built. New on 17 November (Donald, for the build; AA to confirm in OQ-140): each Procedure names its payer, prefilled from the patient, changeable by office or anaesthetist until AUTHORISED, shown in 'Paid by' only where its Contract bills the payer and reading 'not billed yet' before a Contract is chosen. Changing one Procedure's payer offers the same change on the Booking's other Procedures billing that payer (ticked by default, never forced); a Procedure added later copies a shared payer, else starts from the patient. The email-or-postal-address rule and the under-18 warning apply per Procedure, one dashboard to-do per Booking. Procedures billing the same payer share one invoice; a payer typed in separately is a different payer with its own invoice, never matched on name or email. The insurer or funder and approval number stay on the Booking and never decide who is invoiced.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Built in Phase 21 as a Booking field: Booking.payer (BookingPayer, patient or other with BP id and contact; types.ts:259, :812), written only by setBookingPayer (payerActions.ts:134) with a lock once a prepayment invoice has gone to the current payer (:40). Readers are Booking-level: payerCounterparty (whoIsBilled.ts:50), payerContactMissing (:201), childPayerOn (:229), the childPayer warning rule, party picker 'Payer on the Booking' (partyOptions.ts:57). Warning model already supports per-Procedure findings (warnings/types.ts:57). Invoices already group by counterparty ref (invoiceBuild.ts:281), so a distinct payer ref makes its own invoice; prepayment invoices likewise (:396). An edit of the same payer keeps its BP id by a name check (payerActions.ts:150), a separately typed payer gets a new id. No Procedure payer, no offer to copy a change to the others, no 'not billed yet', no copy-on-add rule (bookingActions.ts:411). A post-op addendum is its own linked Booking with its own payer (bookingActions.ts:254).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Rework of the Phase 21 shape. Procedure gains payer (a copied payer keeps its BP id so 'same payer' is identity, never a name match) and Booking.payer goes: 22 non-test files read the payer symbols plus seed bookings, patients and payerReviewBookings. setBookingPayer becomes a Procedure action with an 'also apply to' list; addProcedure and creation paths copy a shared payer; PayerSheet and EditBillingSetupSheet become the 'Paid by' line; contact and under-18 checks run per Procedure (childPayer emits per-Procedure findings, dashboard folds to one per Booking, DM-31); prepayment lock becomes per payer (DM-20); split picker reads the Procedure's payer (DM-28). Invoice grouping needs no new rule. The copy-on-add rule names 'an extra procedure or a post-op addendum': today an addendum is its own Booking (DM-17 replaces it with an event whose billable party defaults to the Procedure's). PERSIST_VERSION bump. Awaits AA (OQ-140) but cheap to build and reverse since today's behaviour is the all-share-one case. Precedes DM-20's per-payer prepayment and DM-28's 'another person' share.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Catalogue (US-11.2.2, US-08.2.1, domain model, 17 Nov change log) says exactly this; none of the cited items is Retired or Future Work. Code re-read: Booking.payer, setBookingPayer, payerCounterparty, partyOptions hint, invoice grouping by refKey (invoiceBuild.ts:281) and prepayment grouping (:396) all as stated. Reader count corrected from 19 to 22 non-test files. Added the post-op addendum wording tension (US-11.2.2 lists an addendum among added Procedures, FT-03.7 makes it an event) to the contradictions list.

dataModelDeltas.title: A split share can name another person, typed with their own name and email or postal address, beside the Procedure's payer, the Contract's holder and other Parties
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: On a Booking the user presses Split against a Procedure and divides its fee between billable parties, each share a typed $ or %, each invoiced its share on its own invoice. New on 17 November (US-08.2.3): a share can name another person with their own name and email or postal address (for example two separated parents), as well as the Procedure's payer, the Contract's holder or another Party. The under-18 warning applies to a share billed to the patient only. It stays a user action, never a Contract setting.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Built in Phase 22: Procedure.split (types.ts:1029; FeeSplit :1049, SplitShare :1042) set by setProcedureSplit (splitActions.ts:60), maths in splitShare.ts, one invoice per share, splitDoesNotFit warning, SplitFeeSheet; funderOverride gone. A share's basis may also be 'the rest'. The party picker (partyOptionsFor, partyOptions.ts:42) offers the Booking's payer, the Contract's party and Parties; no 'another person' option and no typed person on a share. A prepaid Procedure cannot be split (invoiceBuild.ts:352 message, refused at :197 and :409, interim until DM-20).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Small, after DM-11: a share's party gains a typed person (name, relationship, contact, BP id, kept for the debt), the picker adds 'Another person' with the same contact rule, the under-18 check reads a patient share only, and 'payer on the Booking' becomes the Procedure's payer. Invoice grouping unchanged.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-08.2.3 lists exactly the four party kinds and the 'Another person' criterion; code has no typed-person share. Split itself confirmed built. DM-46 previously called DM-28 'built'; reworded there so only the 'another person' share is open here.

dataModelDeltas.title: Price changes become one typed price on the Procedure: the anaesthetist only on an RVG Contract that allows it, or on No contract · Fixed price; the office on any Contract until AUTHORISED (a prepaid price until its invoice is raised); no reason, last change stands
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Each RVG-priced Contract carries an AA-kept setting on whether the anaesthetist may type a price (RVG detail stays recorded); price only, never rate or discount. A fixed price never allows it (OQ-117); a prepaid Contract cannot carry it (OQ-96). Otherwise read-only; the anaesthetist types an amount only on No contract · Fixed price (A37). The office can change any price until AUTHORISED, a prepaid price only until its prepayment invoice is raised (A16). No reason; audited; flagged at review; last change stands; a Contract change clears the typed price. BTM stays recorded when overridden to zero.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Two interim typed-price fields: Procedure.priceOverride (fixedFee, dollarAdjustment, percentAdjustment, each with mandatory reason; types.ts:878, :1020) and enteredPrice (open-price amount; types.ts:967, 21 non-test files). Built since: Contract.anaesthetistMayOverridePrice (contracts.ts:111, seeded on No contract · RVG, not yet acted on), mayTypeEnteredPrice (contractRail.ts:167), typed price beside computed price at review (priceStatus.ts:40). A Contract change already clears BOTH typed values (applyContractChange sets priceOverride and enteredPrice, contractRail.ts:483 to :484); only the 'release the Contract' path (contractSelectionActions.ts:218) clears enteredPrice alone. The override is still writable by anyone through editProcedure (lifecycle.ts:564), OverrideCard, PriceOverrideSheet; no actor gate by the Contract setting, no read-only state after a prepayment invoice.
dataModelDeltas.impact: Collapse priceOverride (with reason) and enteredPrice into one typed price (DM-50's ladder reads it), edited in place with actor audited; gate the anaesthetist on 'RVG Contract AND override setting AND not prepaid' or 'No contract · Fixed price', the office on any Contract unless prepaid and invoiced; the Contract change already clears both fields and must keep clearing the one (the release-Contract path must clear it too); audit labels and review flag move to the one field. 18 non-test files read priceOverride, 21 enteredPrice. Phase 24; depends on DM-10 (built).
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Catalogue held (US-03.5.1, US-05.4.2). Refuted one prototype claim: the draft said priceOverride is not reset on a Contract change, but applyContractChange sets priceOverride: undefined (contractRail.ts:483); only the release path leaves it. Impact reworded accordingly; everything else upheld.

dataModelDeltas.title: A Procedure's price follows its Contract's pricing kind until a person, a prepayment invoice or AUTHORISED holds it: the price ladder and its snapshot rung remain
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Pricing kind decides the price: RVG at anaesthetist's rate, RVG at Contract's rate, RVG less a discount (its own invoice line), fixed price (range in force on the procedure date), open price (typed). Price at any moment, first match wins (US-05.2.8): snapshot once AUTHORISED; prepaid amount once its invoice is raised; a typed price; else derived from the kind; else 'Needs a price', which stops completion and AUTHORISED. Unedited price is derived, not stored; a Contract change clears a typed price; 0 gives a no-charge invoice; ex GST.
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Mostly built: feeFor (fee.ts:239) prices all five kinds and returns needsPrice; the discount is its own invoice line (invoiceBuild.ts:214); priceStatusFor and computedPriceFor (priceStatus.ts:24, :40) feed completion, review flags and 'Needs a price' (Phase 21a). Price computed at the call, never stored. Missing: the typed price is still two fields applied last as replace, $ adjust or % scale (fee.ts:307); no prepaid-amount rung (DM-20); no snapshot rung (DM-08); Method 3 rate x time lines still sum in (fee.ts:291, DM-46).
dataModelDeltas.impact: Narrower than before (five-kind function and typed-amount reset are built). Left: the ladder: one typed-price input replacing override and adjustments, prepaid and snapshot rungs reading DM-20 and DM-08, removal of the rate x time branch with DM-46. feeFor's return shape ripples into invoice builder and capture UI, so do it in one pass with DM-14. Depends on DM-14; precedes DM-08.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: Catalogue and code claims hold. Line reference for the typed-price override block corrected from fee.ts:303 to :307; the Contract-change reset note is now true of both typed fields (see DM-14).

dataModelDeltas.title: Multi-procedure rule: one primary flag, time on every procedure, modifier units split above four
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: Exactly one primary Procedure per Booking, settable by anyone with edit rights. Base units only on the primary; time units on every Procedure from its own times (tiers held as data); modifier units all on the primary while total is 4 or fewer, else split as evenly as possible with remainder to the primary. No Contract changes the rule (OQ-90). Adjusts only RVG-priced Procedures (A19); on a mixed Booking whose primary is fixed or open price, base units go nowhere until OQ-132 is answered (option 1 held).
dataModelDeltas.prototype_has: Time tiers are data (masters.rvgTimeRule, timeUnits.ts) and ordinal-keyed fixed prices are gone with ContractPrice. Still open: Procedure.isAdditional boolean (types.ts:978, 25 non-test files), splitBillingUnits gives additional time only and the rest to the first (fee.ts:139); no settable primary, no modifier split above four, no mixed-Booking rule.
dataModelDeltas.impact: isAdditional becomes isPrimary with 'Make primary'; allocation becomes a pure tested function (base on primary, time everywhere, modifiers split above four, skip fixed or open priced Procedures, mixed-Booking test); feed and capture UI show the primary. Needs DM-44 (built). Phase 23.
dataModelDeltas.verify_note: US-05.3.1 and OQ-132 say this; fee.ts:139 returns time units only for isAdditional and everything else goes to the first Procedure. The catalogue also says the base-unit field is not editable on an additional Procedure, which falls out of the primary flag.

dataModelDeltas.title: Authorising a List snapshots each Procedure's Contract settings and pricing values; the billing engine reads the snapshot
dataModelDeltas.catalogue_says: On AUTHORISED the engine snapshots per Procedure the Contract's settings as then (rate, discount, only the price range in force), the Procedure's values (units, typed price), recorded BTM, unit rate used, price and payer details, so later changes to RVG groups, Contracts or ranges never alter an issued invoice (US-04.3.5, US-08.4.4). A Procedure that 'Needs a price' blocks AUTHORISED (A48). The engine resolves no route or payer. Nothing is relinked.
